task_completion.description: The BraTS T1ce MRI volume is loaded into the 3D Slicer application.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Data' module or 'Volume' selector shows a volume name containing 'BraTS' and 't1ce' or '00000'.

task_completion.description: Volume rendering is activated for the loaded MRI volume.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Volume Rendering' module is open, the visibility (eye icon) is toggled on, and a 3D representation of the brain appears in the 3D view (usually the blue/purple background panel).

task_completion.description: An ROI (Region of Interest) box is created and visible in the 3D view.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A bounding box with colored handles (ROI) is visible surrounding or intersecting the 3D brain volume.

task_completion.description: The 'Display' settings in the Volume Rendering module have 'Clip' enabled.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Clip' checkbox is checked in the Volume Rendering module, and the 3D volume appears cut or sliced where the ROI intersects it.

task_completion.description: The ROI is positioned to remove 30-50% of the brain surface to reveal internal structures.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 3D view shows a significant portion (roughly half) of the brain surface removed, exposing internal cross-sections or tumor structures rather than just the outer shell.

task_completion.description: The agent saves the rendering to the specified file path.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A 'Save' dialog or file browser shows the path '~/Documents/SlicerData/Screenshots/clipped_brain_rendering.png' or a terminal/Python console command confirms the save to that specific path.
